aboutBody.recovery1: Recovery is how ready your body is to take on strain today, on a scale from 1 to 100%.
aboutBody.recovery2: Pulse scores it each morning from your heart rate variability, resting heart rate, respiratory rate, sleep performance and skin temperature, each compared with your own recent baseline.
aboutBody.recovery3: Green (67% and up) means you are primed for a hard day, yellow means maintain, and red means your body is asking for rest.
aboutBody.hrv1: Heart rate variability (HRV) is the variation in time between your heartbeats, measured in milliseconds while you sleep.
aboutBody.hrv2: A higher HRV usually means your nervous system is relaxed and ready for stress; a lower one often follows hard training, poor sleep, alcohol or illness.
aboutBody.hrv3: HRV differs a lot from person to person, so compare it only with your own typical range, not with anyone else's.
aboutBody.rhr1: Resting heart rate (RHR) is how many times your heart beats per minute while you are fully at rest, measured during sleep.
aboutBody.rhr2: A lower RHR generally reflects better fitness and recovery. A rise of a few beats above your typical range can point to fatigue, stress, heat, alcohol or the start of an illness.
aboutBody.resp1: Respiratory rate is how many breaths you take per minute while you sleep.
aboutBody.resp2: It is one of the most stable vitals: night to night it rarely moves much. A clear rise above your typical range is worth noticing, since it often comes with illness or a heavy load on the body.
aboutBody.sleep1: Sleep Performance compares the sleep you got with the sleep your body needed, adjusted for how consistent and efficient that sleep was.
aboutBody.sleep2: Your need rises with yesterday's strain and any sleep debt you carry, so the same hours can score differently on different nights.
aboutBody.hours1: Hours of sleep is the time you actually spent asleep in your main sleep, not counting time awake in bed.
aboutBody.hours2: Most adults need between seven and nine hours, and your own need changes with strain and sleep debt.
aboutBody.hours_need1: Hours vs. needed is the sleep you got as a share of the sleep your body needed that night.
aboutBody.hours_need2: Your need is a baseline plus extra for yesterday's strain and any sleep debt, so a hard day raises it.
aboutBody.restorative1: Restorative sleep is the time you spend in deep (slow-wave) sleep and REM sleep, the two stages where most physical and mental repair happens.
aboutBody.restorative2: Deep sleep comes mostly early in the night and REM mostly late, so a short night cuts REM first.
aboutBody.consistency1: Sleep consistency measures how closely your sleep and wake times match from one day to the next.
aboutBody.consistency2: Going to bed and waking at similar times keeps your body clock steady, which makes the same hours of sleep more restful.
aboutBody.efficiency1: Sleep efficiency is the share of your time in bed that you actually spent asleep: hours of sleep divided by time in bed.
aboutBody.efficiency2: Above 85% is generally considered good. Long spells awake, many wake-ups or a lot of time in bed before falling asleep all lower it.
aboutBody.efficiency3: Better efficiency means more of the night goes to sleep stages that restore you, which also lifts your Sleep Performance.
aboutBody.time_in_bed1: Time in bed runs from when your main sleep started to when it ended, including any time awake.
aboutBody.time_in_bed2: Each bar spans your bedtime to your wake time, so a steady row of bars means a steady schedule.
aboutBody.sleep_stress1: Sleep stress is how much of the night your heart rate and heart rate variability showed a stress response instead of rest.
aboutBody.strain1: Day Strain is the day's load on your heart and body as a percent: 0 to 100 on most days, above 100 on a very big day.
aboutBody.strain2: It builds from the time you spend in higher heart-rate zones and the steps you take while awake, so the climb gets steeper the harder you go.
aboutBody.zones131: Zones 1 to 3 cover light to moderate effort, 50 to 80% of your max heart rate: brisk walks, easy runs, steady rides.
aboutBody.zones132: Time here builds your aerobic base and helps recovery without adding much fatigue.
aboutBody.zones451: Zones 4 and 5 are hard effort, from 80% of your max heart rate: intervals, races and the end of a hard climb.
aboutBody.zones452: A little time here each week raises your fitness ceiling; too much without rest adds strain faster than you recover.
aboutBody.strength1: Strength activity time is the time you spent in resistance training: weights, bodyweight work, CrossFit and similar sessions.
aboutBody.strength2: Regular strength work builds muscle and bone and supports healthy ageing. Most guidelines suggest at least two sessions a week.
aboutBody.steps1: Steps are counted by your Fitbit through the day. They are a simple measure of how much you move outside workouts.
aboutBody.calories1: Calories are everything you burned in the day: your resting burn plus movement and workouts.
aboutBody.vo2max1: VO2 max is the most oxygen your body can use during hard exercise, in millilitres per kilogram of body weight per minute. Fitbit estimates it from your runs, or from your resting heart rate when you don't run.
aboutBody.vo2max2: It is one of the strongest signs of long-term health: higher fitness goes with a longer life. Steady aerobic training raises it over weeks and months.
aboutBody.lean_mass1: Lean body mass is your weight minus your body fat: muscle, bone, organs and water. Pulse works it out from the weight and body fat your scale or the Fitbit app records.
aboutBody.lean_mass2: More lean mass for your height is linked to a longer life, whatever your body fat. Strength training and enough protein build it.

metricAbout.calories: Everything you burned: your resting burn plus movement. Resting is the total minus active calories, since the source sends no separate resting roll-up.
metricAbout.hrv: Variation in time between heartbeats during sleep, measured in milliseconds. Compare it with your own usual range.
metricAbout.rhr: Your resting heart rate as Fitbit reports it to Health Connect, or Pulse's estimate from your night's sleep when Fitbit has none for the day. Recovery and Health Monitor score this same number.
metricAbout.resp: Breaths per minute during sleep, measured by your band.
metricAbout.spo2: Estimated blood oxygen saturation during sleep, measured by your band.
metricAbout.skin: Nightly skin temperature above or below your personal baseline. This is a temperature difference, not your body temperature.
metricAbout.weight: Your weight, from a connected scale or a manual log in your health app.
metricAbout.body_fat: Body fat percentage, from a smart scale or a manual log.
metricAbout.distance: Distance covered on foot and in workouts, from your steps and GPS.
metricAbout.floors: Floors climbed, counted from changes in altitude as you walk.
metricAbout.active_minutes: Minutes of moderate or harder movement, the time that counts toward the 150 minutes a week the WHO recommends.
metricAbout.light_minutes: Minutes of light movement, such as an easy walk or chores.
metricAbout.azm: Active Zone Minutes: a minute in the moderate zone counts once and a minute in the vigorous or peak zones counts twice, toward 150 a week.
metricAbout.active_calories: Calories burned by movement above your resting burn.
metricAbout.sedentary_minutes: Time awake and still: minutes with no steps and a low heart rate, outside sleep and workouts. The hourly view shows your steps: the gaps are when you sat.
metricAbout.avg_hr: Your average heart rate over the whole day, from your band.
metricAbout.water: Water you logged in your health app.
metricAbout.calories_in: Calories from the food you logged.
metricAbout.protein: Protein from the food you logged.
metricAbout.carbs: Carbohydrates from the food you logged.
metricAbout.fat: Fat from the food you logged.
metricAbout.glucose: Blood glucose readings from a connected meter or a manual log.
metricAbout.core_temp: Core body temperature readings from a connected sensor.

metricSource.activity: Your health app's daily roll-up, counted by your band or your phone. Pulse shows it as it comes and does not score it.
metricSource.body: Readings synced from your health app. A day without a reading shows the latest one before it.
metricSource.nutrition: Your health app's daily total of your logs, plus what you log in Pulse's Journal. A meal logged in both Pulse and Fitbit counts once.
metricSource.vitals: Your health app's daily value, from your band or a connected device. Pulse shades your usual range from the last 90 days.
